reviews.quote: The IdeaPad Slim 3 15.3-inch is a convincing affordable laptop: powerful, well-equipped and pleasantly quiet for the money.
An affordable laptop with powerful Ryzen silicon, though cooling limits the Zen 4 CPUs; the stock IPS panel is decent.
A rare miss from Lenovo — the hardware is fine but the price of $769 just feels too high.

praises: Ryzen 7 170 (8C/16T) + 16GB DDR5 is the strongest multicore combo in the whole IdeaPad budget line
Touchscreen at $799.95 is almost unheard of at this size and price
Noticeably snappy in day-to-day use; 7-zip and compile jobs beat the Intel 3i twins
1.59 kg with touch layer — lighter than most non-touch 15" budget laptops
Vega 8 iGPU runs older/esports titles at 720p-1080p low acceptably
complaints: Small ~34Wh battery is the family's worst pairing: an 8-core Zen 3 chip on a 34Wh pack gives ~4h
Fan ramps up loudly on almost any sustained load; benchmark runs are noisy
720p webcam undersells how good the rest of the spec is
Touch layer adds glare and reflections versus the matte non-touch 3i panels
Chassis flex is the same all-plastic Slim 3 story; touch pressing makes lid flex obvious

standouts: Best CPU + RAM + touch combo per dollar in the family — $799.95 buys 8 cores, 16GB and a touchscreen
Only touch option among the seven IdeaPad configs
dealbreakers: 34Wh battery with this chip means realistically commuting with a charger
design_philosophy: The AMD counterweight in Lenovo's budget line: a Zen 3 8-core and 16GB DDR5 in the same thin 15.3" Slim 3 shell, with a touchscreen thrown in to differentiate at retail. The compromise is Lenovo's smallest battery in the family, so mobility is claimed more than delivered.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-ideapad-slim3.md). Inferred from Core 5 320 sibling: +1.2 productivity (8C/16T + 16GB vs 6C/8GB), +0.7 gaming (Vega 8 vs UHD), −1.5 battery (34Wh with a 15W+ chip), thermals −1.7 for known Barcelo heat in thin shells. pen_touch 4.5 = finger touch only, no pen. Panel IPS per BBY spec, 45% NTSC assumed.
